hint: Use the left and right arrow keys to choose a word, the up and down arrow keys to choose a sentence, and the space bar to mark.
announceCheck: Checked: found {found} of {total} errors. Wrongly marked: {wrong}.
toleratedBox: Close enough: {words}. These words are right. They stand in the same sentence right next to a long error. This does not count as a wrong mark.
legendTolerated: close enough (same sentence, next to a long error)
errorClass.real_word: Mistake with a real word (their/there, its/it's)
errorClass.number_name_date: Number, name, date or place changed
sample: Read carefully: 1,234 metres, May 1969, Cologne, Illegal.
tipClasses: Hint: these kinds of errors are in the text this round: {classes}.
tipSentences: Hint: the sentences with an error are marked at the edge, with the kind of error.
praiseHints: You used hints, and that is perfectly fine. Next time you may manage without them.
chooseLead: Here you practise careful reading. What do you want to practise?
kindWhat.text: You get a text, but nothing to compare it with. As when you proofread your own writing, you look for errors you can see in the text itself.
kindWhat.quelle: You get a rendition and its source. As when you check a report, you look for what went wrong when it was passed on.
question.quelle: Does the source really say this?
questionPlus.contradiction: Does it fit what came before?
stagesLead: Choose a stage. Each stage adds new kinds of error, the texts get longer and the help gets less.
cardTextValue: about {wordsFrom} to {wordsTo} words in {sentencesFrom} to {sentencesTo} sentences
helpTip.none: No reading tip first, only on request.
helpMaterial.sheet: The excerpt of the source comes as a sheet of its own.
helpMaterial.link: The source is the real article, as a link. You find the passage yourself.
helpNamed: The task names the kinds of error.
helpHidden: The task does not name the kinds of error.
tip.text.1: Read slowly, word by word. Say the words in your head.
tip.text.2: Stop briefly at every word: is a letter missing? Is a word there twice?
tip.text.3: Look at every end of a sentence and every comma.
tip.quelle.1: Read the source first. Remember numbers, names and places.
tip.quelle.2: Then read the rendition sentence by sentence. After each sentence, go back to the source.
tip.quelle.3: Other words are not an error yet. Ask yourself: does the source say the same?
goalNamed: {count} errors are hidden in this text. These kinds occur: {classes}.
goalHidden: {count} errors are hidden in this text. You find out which kinds yourself.
sheetRendition: Rendition: mark what does not match the source
renditionNote: The rendition says some things in other words. That is not an error.
linkHeading: The source is the real article.
linkText: Open it and find the passages the text is about.
linkStand: You see the version of {date}. The top of the page may say that it is an older version. That is as it should be.
linkPdf: Article not reachable or different? Open the source as a PDF
announceBegin: Here we go. {count} errors are hidden.
praiseClean: Great! You found every error and marked nothing that was right. That was very careful reading.
praiseAll: Great! You found every error. Look below at what else was marked.
adviceLast: That was the hardest stage. Why not try the other exercise too.
adviceAgain: Try another round at this stage.
adviceBetter: Well found. Next time, try to mark fewer words that are right.
adviceOvermarked: You marked a lot that is right. Other words are not an error yet. At every sentence ask yourself: does the source say the same?
adviceNoTip: Tip: Read even more slowly and mark only where you are sure.
noSource: This sentence is not in the source.
wrongBox.text: Marked wrongly: {words}. These words are right. Read slowly once more before you mark anything.
wrongBox.quelle: Marked wrongly: {words}. These words are right. Compare them with the source before you mark anything.
basis.comparison: visible only by comparing with the source
classTip.spelling_rule: Say the word slowly. Does a related word help (hit – hitting)?
classTip.slip: Read word by word: is a letter missing, is a word there twice?
classTip.real_word: The word exists, but does it fit here? Watch their/there and its/it's.
classTip.punctuation: Look at every end of a sentence and every comma.
classTip.contradiction: At every sentence ask: does it fit what came before?
classTip.number_name_date: Compare every number, every name and every place with the source.
classTip.factual_error: Does the source give this exact detail?
classTip.added_claim: Does the source say this at all? Some sentences are made up.
classTip.connective_negation: Watch the small words: not, no, but, so.
classTip.quantity_degree: Watch the amounts: some, many, all, often, always.
classTip.faulty_inference: Does one thing after another become "because" or "so"?
classTip.opinion_as_fact: Is this a fact from the source or an opinion?
classTip.false_authority: Who says so? Does the source name these experts?
classTip.loaded_language: Does the rendition sound more judging than the source?
